# Exploratory analysis

Goals

- Identify the best threshold to remove noise; improve quantitative predictions from ML

- plotting distributions

```{r loadStuff}
library(tidyverse, quietly = TRUE)
library(magrittr) # for special Tee pipe operator %T>% (Error check, unique WT before calc)

# import functions
source("functions/0.data_processing.R")
source("functions/1.plotting.R")

# locate the data
base_path <- "enrichment_data/theoAptzepPCR_lokya/"
# file_path <- str_c(base_path, "subset.tsv") # for testing
file_path <- str_c(base_path, "DiMSum_Project_variant_data_merge.tsv") # for production
```
## Data cleanup
- Select relevant columns
- Clean up column names
- Calculate enrichment, leak metrics
Ref: _Borrowing some code from DiMSum/[split-multiinputs.R](https://github.com/ppreshant/DiMSum/blob/master/scripts/split_multiinputs.R) 

```{r data-cleanup}
data <- read_and_cleanup_data(file_path)
cat("Column names: ", paste(colnames(data), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```


## Visualizations
```{r raw_count_distribution}
#| fig-width: 2
#| fig-height: 3

# nham_variant_count_distribution(head(data, 1000)) # top 1,000 data
nham_variant_count_distribution(data) # all data
```



Looking at the distribution of Nham_nt counts, we can see that there are a lot of variants with low counts. We want to filter out these low-count variants to reduce noise in our analysis.

## Filtering variants with counts >= 2
```{r threshold_test}
#| fig-width: 2
#| fig-height: 3

d2 <- data |> filter(if_any(matches("count"), \(ct) ct >= 2))
nham_variant_count_distribution(d2)
```

## Testing annotation placement
```{r dummy-test}
#| fig-width: 2
#| fig-height: 3

library(grid) # for plotting advanced: textGrob etc.
dummy <- tibble(x = 1:10, y = x^2)

# testing static position of annotation (figure out x/xmax and y/ymin)
# ref: https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/annotation_custom.html
ggplot(dummy, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() + labs(title = "Dummy plot") + 
  annotation_custom(grob = textGrob(str_c("snps: ", snp_count), hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, gp = gpar(size = 3)), 
                  xmax = 0, ymin = 0)

```
